name: @chrischall/pickuppatrol-mcp

tools.name: pup_get_session
tools.description: The signed-in PickUp Patrol parent account: name, email, last sign-in, and the students linked to it. Start here to discover student and school ids.

tools.name: pup_list_students
tools.description: Every student on the account, each with their weekly default dismissal plan and whether those defaults still need a parent review.

tools.name: pup_get_student
tools.description: One student in full, including the default dismissal plan for each weekday. Pass raw: true for the untouched API record.

raw.description: Return the unprojected API record instead of the summary

tools.name: pup_healthcheck
tools.description: Verify the configured credentials sign in and the PickUp Patrol API answers. Reports the server version, the students the account can see, and — when it fails — an error.kind saying which hop broke: no_credential (nothing configured), credential_rejected (PickUp Patrol refused the username/password), verification_pending (a two-factor account), edge_blocked (a CDN/WAF refused the request before PickUp Patrol saw it, so the credentials were never judged), timeout, transport or http. Read-only; never returns the credentials.

tools.name: pup_list_transportations
tools.description: The dismissal options a school offers (bus, car pickup, walker, absent …) with the rules each one imposes: whether a note is required, whether it takes a car number, whether it is an early dismissal, and the daily cutoff time. Read this before setting a plan.

include_inactive.description: Include options the school has deactivated (default false)

tools.name: pup_get_school
tools.description: A school profile together with its per-weekday notify times and plan cutoff times, and the settings that decide whether parents may set plans at all.

tools.name: pup_list_non_school_days
tools.description: Dates a plan cannot be set for at a school (holidays, closures, weekends), and optionally the dates in a range that already differ from the student defaults.

start_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD; with end_date, also return dates that differ from the default

tools.name: pup_list_car_numbers
tools.description: The car numbers a school has issued to this account, for dismissal options where usesCarNumbers is true.

tools.name: pup_list_plans
tools.description: Day-by-day dismissal plans across a date range for every student on the account, as PickUp Patrol returns them.

tools.name: pup_get_plan
tools.description: The dismissal plan for one student on one date — the option in force, any note, the early-dismissal time, and whether the date is locked because the cutoff has passed.

tools.name: pup_set_plan
tools.description: Change how a student is dismissed on one or more specific dates, or clear those dates back to the student's weekly default. This changes how a child actually leaves school. Asks the user to confirm first: a confirmation prompt where the client supports one; otherwise the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and only a repeat call with that token proceeds (see MCP_CONFIRM_MODE). The preview shows the exact payload. Read pup_list_transportations first — options differ in whether they require a note, a car number or an early-dismissal time.

dates.description: One or more YYYY-MM-DD dates to apply this plan to

transportation_id.description: Dismissal option id from pup_list_transportations, or null to clear these dates back to the student's default plan

note.description: Note for the school; required by some options

early_dismissal_time.description: HH:MM, required when the option is an early dismissal

car_number.description: Car number, for options where usesCarNumbers is true

confirmToken.description: ONLY for the two-step confirmation fallback (a client without MCP elicitation). The confirmToken from this same tool's phase-1 "confirmation-required" response, passed back ONLY after the user has seen that preview and explicitly approved it in chat — never on the first call, never invented, never reused. Call again with the same arguments. Ignored when the client supports elicitation.

tools.name: pup_get_default_plans
tools.description: A student's weekly default dismissal plan — how they normally leave school on each day of the week — and whether the defaults still need a parent review.

tools.name: pup_set_default_plans
tools.description: Change a student's weekly default dismissal plan for one or more weekdays, or clear every default. This is how the child leaves school on any date without a specific plan. Asks the user to confirm first: a confirmation prompt where the client supports one; otherwise the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and only a repeat call with that token proceeds (see MCP_CONFIRM_MODE). Read pup_list_transportations first.

days.description: Weekdays to change, as names ("Monday") or ids (1 = Sunday … 7 = Saturday)

note.description: Note for the school; required by some options

early_dismissal_time.description: HH:MM, required when the option is an early dismissal

clear_all.description: Remove every weekday default instead of setting one (days is ignored)

confirmToken.description: ONLY for the two-step confirmation fallback (a client without MCP elicitation). The confirmToken from this same tool's phase-1 "confirmation-required" response, passed back ONLY after the user has seen that preview and explicitly approved it in chat — never on the first call, never invented, never reused. Call again with the same arguments. Ignored when the client supports elicitation.

tools.name: pup_mark_defaults_reviewed
tools.description: Mark a student's default plans as reviewed, clearing the school's 'needs review' prompt. Asks the user to confirm first: a confirmation prompt where the client supports one; otherwise the first call returns a preview and a confirmToken, and only a repeat call with that token proceeds (see MCP_CONFIRM_MODE).

confirmToken.description: ONLY for the two-step confirmation fallback (a client without MCP elicitation). The confirmToken from this same tool's phase-1 "confirmation-required" response, passed back ONLY after the user has seen that preview and explicitly approved it in chat — never on the first call, never invented, never reused. Call again with the same arguments. Ignored when the client supports elicitation.
